purpose: Specification-first contract for the four corrective backend domains authorized by COR-UI08-001. This artifact is the authority the Increment 2b contract tests assert against, and the authority Increments 3-6 implement to. It is deterministic and carries no wall-clock field so it supports --check.

authority_notes.openapi: docs/api/openapi.json is DERIVED from the live route collection by servana:openapi (dedoc/scramble) and is never hand-written. The specification-first artifact for API operations is therefore this matrix; openapi.json is regenerated once per domain as its routes land, and Ui08CorrectiveContractMatrixTest asserts matrix<->OpenAPI parity for every operation whose implementation_state is 'implemented'.
authority_notes.operation_id: An operationId in this repository IS the route name (verified across all 302 baseline operations). Every operation_id below is therefore also the route name to register.
authority_notes.migration_manifest: MigrationManifestTest fails when a manifest entry references a migration file that does not exist, so manifest.yaml entries are authored in the same increment as their migration files. The proposed-migration records live here (migration_plan) and are the 'manifest before migration' authority required by ADR-004 section 6; the data-dictionary entries were authored first, in Increment 2b, before any migration file exists.
authority_notes.route_group: All 33 operations register inside the existing routes/api.php platform group: prefix('platform') with auth:sanctum, EnforceIdleTimeout, EnsureActivePrincipal, throttle:api, EnsurePrivilegedMfa, ResolvePlatformContext. That group forbids ResolveTenantContext and EnsureMerchantActive (RouteClass::PlatformMutation), which is what keeps a merchant tenant context off every one of them.

expected_after_all_four_domains.note: No permission key is added by any of the four domains beyond the two internal-access keys already added in Increment 2a.

read.route_class_note: Reads carry no RouteClassification default, matching every existing platform read (platform.merchants.index, platform.settings.show). RouteSecurityContractTest only classifies mutations.

shared_route_security.error_envelope: Plan section 11.5 structured envelope; 403 permission_denied, 422 validation_failed / invalid_state_transition, 404 for a foreign or unknown ULID (non-enumerating), 409 idempotency_conflict.
shared_route_security.pagination: Every collection paginates with a bounded page size and an allowlisted sort vocabulary.

step_up_actions.rationale: COR-UI08-001 requires fresh step-up on every /platform-access mutation. StepUpAction is the central registry (Plan section 18), so a live route must carry its own classification rather than borrow billing_configuration, which would make the step-up assertion untraceable to the action it protects.
COR-UI08-001 requires fresh step-up on every production-sensitive feature-flag change including the emergency pause path.

domains.action_note: Approve, reject and cancel share ONE action (DecideFeatureFlagChange) because they share the pending-lock and history-append obligations; approval additionally applies the configuration in the same transaction. A separate change-request state machine class proved unnecessary - the transitions are enforced by the pending lock plus the database CHECKs, and a second class would have restated them without adding a guarantee.

migration_plan.purpose: The single effective-dated SMS pricing authority, proven necessary because platform_billing_settings rows are complete configuration snapshots written by two authorities at now(), so a future-dated SMS row would silently revert unrelated billing settings.
migration_plan.backfill: one genesis rule from config('sms.pricing.unit_cost_minor') at effective_from 2026-07-22T00:00:00Z, so the entire existing sms_billing_entries history resolves to the rule that actually produced its snapshots
migration_plan.application_compatibility: expand-only; SmsCostCalculator continues to answer identically because the genesis rule carries the same configured unit cost
migration_plan.rollback_strategy: forward-repair only (ADR-004): schedule a corrective rule. The table is append-only, so no destructive rollback exists or is needed.
migration_plan.data_retention_impact: none — pricing configuration, no personal data
migration_plan.security_impact: moves SMS pricing from deployment configuration to a versioned, audited, MFA + step-up governed authority. Strictly stronger.

migration_plan.purpose: Lifecycle authority for internal platform access; users.is_platform_staff is a bare boolean with no status, actor, reason or timestamps.
migration_plan.backfill: one active membership per existing users.is_platform_staff = true row, so the flag and the membership agree from the first migration onwards
migration_plan.application_compatibility: expand-only; every shipped reader of is_platform_staff keeps working unchanged
migration_plan.data_retention_impact: identity-adjacent lifecycle record; retained with the identity
migration_plan.security_impact: adds accountability where a bare boolean previously carried none

migration_plan.purpose: Magic Link-compatible platform invitation; staff_invitations cannot carry it (NOT NULL merchant_id/branch_id, role CHECK excludes super_admin).
migration_plan.data_retention_impact: holds a normalized email and a token HASH only; the raw token is never persisted
migration_plan.security_impact: hashed, single-use, expiring, purpose- and environment-bound credential

migration_plan.purpose: Deny-only platform overrides; merchant_user_permission_overrides is keyed on merchant_user_id and cannot address a platform administrator.
enums_checks: scope-guard trigger rejecting any permission whose permissions.category <> 'platform'
migration_plan.application_compatibility: expand-only; PermissionResolver::forPlatformStaff subtracts denies once the table exists
migration_plan.security_impact: makes self-escalation and merchant-key assignment structurally unrepresentable

migration_plan.purpose: Administrator-initiated session revocation needs a truthful reason; the closed vocabulary has none (session_revoked_by_owner and global_logout both describe the user's own action).
enums_checks: replaces both revoked_reason CHECK constraints, adding exactly platform_access_sessions_revoked
migration_plan.backfill: none — existing rows keep their existing reasons
migration_plan.application_compatibility: widening a CHECK is backward compatible; older code simply never writes the new value. The shipped UI-03 migrations are NOT edited (guardrail 12).
migration_plan.rollback_strategy: forward-repair only; narrowing again would require no rows to hold the value

migration_plan.purpose: Per-environment flag state. No existing table carries a rollout state machine, and config alone cannot record who changed what, when, under which approval.
migration_plan.backfill: none — an empty production catalogue is truthful and is never padded
migration_plan.application_compatibility: expand-only; an absent row evaluates deny

migration_plan.purpose: Closed-vocabulary targeting rows so a rollout can be scoped to a merchant, plan or cohort without ever persisting an executable predicate.
migration_plan.security_impact: closed type vocabulary + scalar value means no executable predicate is storable

migration_plan.purpose: Maker/checker workflow for production-sensitive flag changes, with mandatory impact, rollback plan and health criterion, and a database CHECK that makes self-approval unrepresentable.
migration_plan.security_impact: self-approval becomes unrepresentable at the database

migration_plan.purpose: Append-only before/after history with configuration hashes, actor, reason and correlation ID, giving flag governance the same immutability guarantee audit_logs has.
enums_checks: append-only trigger raising on UPDATE and DELETE
